source_class: user annotated rear photograph plus previously captured DSI506 dimensions and FFC measurements
proposal: Mount the Pajoniiir-M1 custom mainboard directly to the four inner rear threaded-post locations on the display module, keeping the mainboard parallel to the display rear PCB.

mount_pattern.source: inner four DSI506 mounting locations identified in the dimensioned rear drawing and user annotated photograph
mount_pattern.board_hole_pattern_policy: If the post thread and seating surfaces are verified suitable, the M1 mainboard shall use this exact 58 x 49 mm four-hole datum as its primary display-relative mounting pattern.

ffc.routing_concept: Use a controlled U-bend near the display right edge and place the M1 host DSI receptacle in the corresponding right-side region. Exact host connector XY/Z remains open until the post seating plane and FFC bend envelope are measured.
ffc.length_screen: 60 mm is favorable for a direct-behind-display mainboard concept, but no production bend radius or slack claim is made until physical mock-up / bend-envelope measurement.

mainboard_orientation_candidate.display_facing_side_policy: Keep substantially component-free to minimize collision risk; the host DSI receptacle may be an intentional exception if the measured inter-board gap and assembly sequence pass.
assembly_sequence_candidate: pre-insert FFC into the display-side host receptacle if access requires it
seat mainboard on the four verified posts
route FFC through the approved U-bend without twist or over-folding

why_preferred: Uses existing display-relative mechanical datums instead of introducing independent enclosure standoffs.
Keeps display-to-mainboard alignment deterministic and repeatable.
Can reduce enclosure complexity and tolerance stack-up.
The 58 x 49 mm pattern is central enough to support a mainboard larger than the pattern while still allowing connector overhang toward enclosure walls.
The display DSI receptacle is close to the right edge, which is favorable for a short controlled FFC return path to a mainboard mounted directly behind the module.
hard_gates_before_lock: verify all four marked posts are actually available threaded mounting points and are coplanar
measure thread type / screw major diameter
measure usable thread depth or safe screw engagement
measure post seating-plane Z above the display rear PCB
confirm whether the previously measured 10.0 mm maximum rear protrusion is the top of these four posts
measure post outside diameter / washer-bearing surface
confirm the display assembly tolerates the added mainboard mass and screw preload without stressing the LCD stack
create a local XY obstruction map for display-side components under the candidate mainboard
validate the 60 mm FFC bend path and mating keepout with the selected mainboard Z plane
identify display receptacle pin 1 and prove host pin 1 to module pin 1 mapping
do_not_infer: Do not assume M2, M2.5 or any other screw thread from the photograph.
Do not assume the 10 mm Z measurement is the post top until the user confirms what feature was measured.
Do not freeze the mainboard outline from the 58 x 49 mm hole pattern alone.
Do not place tall components on the display-facing side before the obstruction map is established.
